[Response]

Light absorption: Plants absorb light energy from the sun using chlorophyll, a pigment found in organelles called chloroplasts.  2. Water splitting: The absorbed light energy is used to power a process called photolysis, which splits water molecules into oxygen gas and hydrogen ions.  3. Carbon fixation: The hydrogen ions are used to convert carbon dioxide into a usable form, while the oxygen gas is released as a byproduct.  4. Reduction: The carbon dioxide is reduced to a molecule containing carbon and a high-energy electron, which is then used to produce glucose and other sugars.

user: What are the security implications of configuring non-HTTP/HTTPS traffic for global load balancers?
assistant:  I don't have specific information on the security implications of configuring non-HTTP/HTTPS traffic for global load balancers.
user: What exactly the global load balancers do and any subscription  available?
assistant: Global load balancers help distribute network or application traffic across multiple locations or regions. IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) is an example of a global load balancer provider, offering features like Global Load Balancer (GLB), Caching, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Page rules. They help to ensure reliability and performance by directing traffic to the most available and responsive endpoints. As for subscriptions, IBM CIS offers various plans, including a Free Trial plan with limited features and Standard paid plans with additional capabilities. You can refer to the IBM Cloud website for the most current and detailed information on their subscription options.

user: How frequently do you do a health check in the back-end? and is there any limitations?
assistant: Health checks in IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) are done periodically to monitor the availability of origin servers. The frequency of these health checks is every 15 seconds. However, the default retry rate is 5 retries per second, which can be configured. It is not recommended to increase the retry rate significantly as retries use exponential backoff.
Regarding limitations, it is important to note that health checks for deleted pools and origins cannot be filtered, but they still appear in the table. Also, when adding the request header name for a health check, use 'Host' with a capitalized 'H'. Using a lower-case 'host' for a health check will fail.

user: how do you distribute among bare-metal and virtual-server instances?  Multiple policies ok?
assistant: The IBM Cloud Load Balancer service distributes traffic among multiple server instances, including bare-metal and virtual-server instances, by using Layer 7 (application layer) data. Layer 7 load balancing is supported for HTTP and HTTPS traffic only. Multiple policies can be associated with a front-end port, and these policies are evaluated in order, based on the priority assigned to each policy. Each Layer 7 rule is associated with a policy, and if all the rules that are associated with the policy evaluate to true, the policy is matched, so the associated action is taken.
For more information, see [L7 Policy and Rules](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/loadbalancer-service?topic=loadbalancer-service-layer-7-policy).

user: If not, what wd happen?
assistant: If you refer to the scenario where multiple policies are not associated with a front-end port in the IBM Cloud Load Balancer service, then the system might not be able to apply the appropriate actions to the data traffic. 
user: Then do I lose all the traffic?  any remedy?

[Response]
No—if you mean that an incoming request does not match any policy, it is not automatically lost. The system redirects it to the configured HTTPS redirect listener, if present; otherwise, it redirects it to the listener’s default pool. [S6]

The remedy is to check that the intended fallback—your HTTPS redirect listener or default pool—is configured appropriately. You can also adjust policy rules: a policy applies only when all its rules match. Multiple policies can be attached to a listener, but each must have a different priority. [S3][S4][S5]
